Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

$$P\times_G F=(P\times F)/\bigl((pg,x)\sim(p,gx)\bigr)$$
with the ordinary quotient topology, and write $[p,x]$ for its points. Precisely, the relation is the orbit relation of the right action $(p,x)\cdot g=(pg,g^{-1}x)$. Its action law is $((p,x)\cdot g)\cdot h=(pgh,h^{-1}g^{-1}x)=(p,x)\cdot(gh)$, and its generating relations are exactly the displayed ones. The projection $r([p,x])=\pi(p)$ is well-defined and continuous by [[thm-quotient-universal-property]], since $(p,x)\mapsto\pi(p)$ is continuous and constant on every orbit. Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $s\ge1$,
$n_i\ge1$ and $N_i\ge n_i+1$ for $1\le i\le s$, let $k$ be a field, and put
$$U_N=\prod_{i=1}^{s}\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad r_N=2\min_{i}(N_i-n_i),$$
where $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is the open set of
injective, equivalently full-rank, complex $N\times n$ matrices. Then:

1. each $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is homotopy equivalent to
   the Stiefel space $V_n(\mathbb C^N)=\{A\in\mathbb C^{N\times n}:A^*A=I_n\}$
   of orthonormal frames
   ([[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]]);
2. each $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is a compact path-connected smooth manifold and is
   homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and the map
   $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ forgetting the last column is a
   numerable locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $S^{2(N-n)+1}$, hence a
   Hurewicz and a Serre fibration;
3. $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$.

GL-equivariance of the retractions or trivializations below is asserted.

and
[[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]]:
$S$ and $Y$ are the analytic spaces of separated finite-type complex varieties,
$Y$ trivializes over charts $V$ of $S$ carrying the finite conical cochain

connected finite-type smooth fiber $F$ carries a finite deleted-boundary model.

vanishes in degrees $1,\dots,r$: $H^0(F;k)=k$ and $H^j(F;k)=0$ for

pushforward of every bounded algebraically constructible complex considered
below again has bounded algebraically constructible cohomology, with the finite
models supplied by the two named lemmas. Then, for bounded algebraically

1. for $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ belongs to

2. pullback induces an isomorphism

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.

Assume AC. For a strict augmented simplicial space $Z_\bullet\to S$, its category of simplicial analytic $k$-sheaves has explicit coinduced injective resolutions. The derived augmentation is computed by the normalized double complex with first page $R^j q_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every total-degree diagonal finite. The same construction works for strict bisimplicial diagrams and is compatible with composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse image. If $Z_\bullet$ is the Čech nerve of a map $P\to S$ admitting local sections, inverse image gives an equivalence from $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ to the full derived subcategory with Cartesian cohomology. Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of

variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_p\to Z_m$. The maps $q_p:Z_p\to X$,
$q_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=g_1\cdots g_px$, satisfy $q_p\circ Z_\alpha=q_m$ for
every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ and augment $Z_\bullet$ over the constant
simplicial space $X$.

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_m\to F_p$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_m)\to H^j(A_p)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

The derived category, with shift $[1]$ and distinguished triangles the isomorphic images of cone triangles, is triangulated. The localization functor $Q$ is exact. Every such triangle gives a long exact cohomology sequence $\cdots\to H^n(X)\to H^n(Y)\to H^n(Z)\to H^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The frame bundle and its nerve.** By [F1] the map $U_N\to B_N$ is a locally trivial principal $G$-bundle with algebraic graph-chart sections, the action on $U_N$ is free, and $X_N=(U_N\times X)/G$ is the associated bundle with local charts $V\times X$; the quotient map $q_N:P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N$ is the associated bundle projection. The nerve $G^\bullet\times P_N$ is the Čech nerve of $q_N$, so [F5] applies to it. The simplicial map $p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$ is $(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$ in every degree; in degree $m$ it is the projection $G^m\times U_N\times X\to G^m\times X$, a trivial fiber bundle with fiber $U_N$ and constructible product charts $V\times U_N$; this is the action nerve and ambient simplicial category of [F6].

**The fiber is $r_N$-acyclic with finite models.** By [F2], $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$, and the product of Stiefel models supplies the bounded finite cochain model of the fiber with coefficient-field compatibility. By [F4] the base $G^m\times X$ carries the finite conical cochain models, so each levelwise projection of step 1.1 is a locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting with $r_N$-acyclic fiber.

**The levelwise cone bound.** Fix $m$ and put $p_{N,m}=p_N$ in degree $m$. For $B_m\in D_c^{\ge b}(G^m\times X;k)$ the cone of the unit $B_m\to Rp_{N,m*}p_{N,m}^*B_m$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r_N+1}$ by [F3] applied in the setting of step 2.1. Because $Rp_{N,m*}$ is computed levelwise and cohomological bounds of complexes of simplicial sheaves are decided levelwise, the cone of the unit $B\to Rp_{N*}p_N^*B$ in the simplicial derived category lies in $D^{\ge b+r_N+1}$ as well.

**The simplicial Hom comparison.** The simplicial category has the exact levelwise inverse image $p_N^*$ left adjoint to the levelwise direct image $Rp_{N*}$ and carries the canonical t-structure of [F7], whose aisles are defined cohomology-objectwise and hence are the levelwise aisles. With the cone bound of step 3.1 in place, the argument of [F3] — its Hom comparison, image criterion, full faithfulness and its retract and extension clauses — applies verbatim inside the simplicial bounded derived category: for $A\in D^{\le a}$ and $B\in D^{\ge b}$ the long exact Hom sequence of the unit triangle and the orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\le a},D^{\ge a+1})=0$ identify the pullback map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m'])\to\operatorname{Hom}(p_N^*A,p_N^*B[m'])$ as an isomorphism for $m'\le b+r_N-a$; for $a-b\le r_N$ it is fully faithful on the full subcategory $D^{[b,a]}$; and on that interval an object lies in the image exactly when the truncated counit $p_N^*\tau^{\le a}Rp_{N*}C\to C$ is an isomorphism, the image being closed under retracts and under extensions when $r_N\ge a-b+1$. Every input of that argument is an input already verified here: the adjunction and levelwise model [F5], the cone bound of step 3.1, and the t-structure orthogonality [F7].

**Descent and the functor $Q_N$.** Restricting the conclusion of step 4.1 to the full subcategory of Cartesian objects identified with $D_c^b(X_N;k)$ by [F5], the functor $p_N^*$ followed by descent is $Q_N$: for $F\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ the object $p_N^*F$ has Cartesian cohomology because $p_N$ is a simplicial map and the structure squares of $p_N^*$ are Cartesian by naturality of inverse image; descent produces $Q_N(F)\in D_c^b(X_N;k)$, and $q_N^*Q_N(F)\cong p_N^*F$ canonically. Hence, for $A\le a$, $B\ge b$ and $m\le b+r_N-a$, the isomorphisms of step 4.1 compose with the descent equivalence to give $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$, proving claim 1; the same composition proves claim 2 on intervals of width at most $r_N$.

**The image.** Let $H\in D_c^{[b,a]}(X_N;k)$ with $a-b\le r_N$. By the characterization of step 4.1 applied to $C=q_N^*H$, the object $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of $p_N^*$ on $D_c^{[b,a]}(G^\bullet\times X;k)$ if and only if $p_N^*\tau^{\le a}Rp_{N*}q_N^*H\to q_N^*H$ is an isomorphism, and this is an isomorphism exactly on the objects glued from $X$ by descent; equivalently $H$ lies in the image of $Q_N$ precisely when $q_N^*H$ is the pullback of an object of $D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)$, which is the resolution-triple description: an object of $D_c^{[b,a]}(X_N;k)$ together with an isomorphism $q_N^*H\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ for some $F\in D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)$. Closure under retracts and, for $r_N\ge a-b+1$, under extensions follows from the corresponding clauses of step 4.1 and the exactness and conservativity of $q_N^*$ in descent; this proves claim 3.

**Coherence and the trivial group.** The product $U_N\times U_M$ is a free smooth $G$-resolution in its own right. Its projections to $U_N$ and $U_M$ descend to $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$, locally trivial bundles with fibres $U_M$ and $U_N$. Their pullbacks are fully faithful on the stated intervals by [F3] and the bounds $r_M,r_N$. On the common principal bundle $U_N\times U_M\times X$, both pulled-back representatives have the canonical descent identification with the same pullback of $A$ from $X$; these identifications are compatible with the principal-bundle nerve maps, so [F5]'s descent equivalence yields a canonical isomorphism $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)\simeq\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$. Naturality is inherited from those same inverse-image and descent maps. On the triple product all comparisons identify the representatives with the same pullback of $A$, so their two compositions agree and the cocycle law follows. This compares objects and Hom maps in the common category, without equating the two different target categories or identifying the product with a larger frame space. If $G$ is trivial, take the point as its resolution; then $X_N=X$, the action nerve is constant at $X$, $r_N=\infty$ and $Q_N$ is the identity. This proves claims 4 and 5.

**Conclusion.** Steps 3.1 to 5.1 prove claims 1 and 2, step 6.1 claim 3, and step 7.1 claims 4 and 5. The comparison is used only on the nerve and through the finite local models: no global splitting of $Ra_{N*}a_N^*B$ is asserted, so genuine characteristic-class transgressions are preserved. AC enters only through [A1].

boundaries.evidence: For empty X the associated variety X_N is empty, all equivariant and ordinary Hom groups in claims 1 and 2 vanish, and the assertions of steps 4.1 and 5.1 hold trivially; no nonempty hypothesis is used.

The case m=0 of claim 1 is the degree-zero ring comparison, obtained in step 4.1 and used in step 5.1; the zero interval width a=b is the smallest case of claims 2 and 3 and is included in the width bound a-b at most r_N.
The trivial-group case is claim 5, proved in step 7.1: then U_N and B_N are a point, X_N is X, r_N is infinite and Q_N is the identity of D_c^b(X;k).

The degenerate resolution N_i=n_i+1 at the boundary of the allowed range is covered by step 2.1: the fiber U_N still carries the finite cohomology-gap model with parameter r_N at least 2, so the comparison ranges are nonempty.

The two endpoint regimes are separated: step 4.1 proves the Hom comparison exactly up to m=b+r_N-a and full faithfulness for width a-b at most r_N, while step 6.1 asserts extension closure only for the strict endpoint r_N at least a-b+1.

Step 8.1 records the AC audit: choice enters only through the injective replacements, finite models and Serre-spectral-sequence supplier of [A1]; the frame charts, descent geometry and image argument are otherwise choice-free.

The forward direction of the image description in claim 3 is proved in step 6.1: if H is in the image of Q_N then q_N^*H is the pullback of an object of D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k), i.e. a resolution triple whose frame pullback comes from X.

The reverse direction is proved in step 6.1 through the truncated-counit characterization of step 4.1: if q_N^*H comes from X, the counit is an isomorphism and descent produces an equivariant object mapping to H.

$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_m\to F_p$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_m)\to H^j(A_p)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological
space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space
$(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$
([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally
small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and
iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific
injective resolution
([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). These resolutions are
bounded-below injective replacements, so with the dependent choice supplied by
AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below
injective complexes model the bounded derived category:
$K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to
D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence, and morphisms of the bounded
derived category are computed by these replacements
([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let
$\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier
condition of $X$
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded
and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$
([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under
shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded
algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one
common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is
bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. No general local-smallness theorem for unbounded $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $G$ acts on $U_N$ by precomposition of frames and on $U_N\times X$
diagonally, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$, $B_N$ and $X_N$ are $X$
   or a point, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

No global tensor splitting
$Ra_{N*}a_N^*B\simeq B\otimes_kR\Gamma(U_N;k)$ is asserted for the
frame-bundle projection $a_N:P_N\to B_N$; the comparison is used only on the
nerve and through the finite local models.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The ambient category and its Hom groups.** By [F1] the category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ is abelian with levelwise exactness, has enough injectives under AC via the coinduced objects $N_pI$, and its bounded derived category is actual with set-sized Hom groups computed by bounded-below injective replacements. This is the ambient category of the definition, with the ordinary shift and cone triangles of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

**Closure under the triangulated operations.** Shifts and isomorphisms preserve Cartesian cohomology and the constructibility of the degree-zero restriction because the structure maps of a shifted or isomorphic complex are the shifts or conjugates of the original structure maps. For a cone $C(f)$ of a morphism $f:A\to B$ of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$, the structure maps of $C(f)$ are the cones of the levelwise structure maps, and exactness of simplicial inverse image identifies the structural comparison for $C(f)$ with the map of cones of the structural comparisons for $A$ and $B$. Those two comparisons are quasi-isomorphisms by Cartesianity, so their cone comparison is a quasi-isomorphism by the long exact cohomology sequences. Thus $C(f)$ has Cartesian cohomology. The degree-zero restriction $C(f)_0$ is the cone of $f_0$ between constructible complexes, and by the common-stratification closure of [F2] it is again constructible. Hence $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a full triangulated subcategory of the ambient bounded derived category.

**Conservative restriction.** Let $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with $A_0\cong0$ in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. All cohomology sheaves of $A_0$ vanish, and by Cartesianity the structure morphism of $H^j(A)$ along the projection $d_0^p:Z_p\to Z_0=X$ identifies $H^j(A)_p$ with the pullback of $H^j(A_0)$ for every $p$, so every cohomology simplicial sheaf of $A$ vanishes. An object of the bounded derived category with vanishing cohomology objects is zero by [F2], so $A\cong0$. Restriction to $X$ is thus conservative.

**The finite resolution triples.** Apply [F3] to the frame resolution of $G$: the simplicial map $p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$ is levelwise a locally trivial bundle with $r_N$-acyclic fiber, its induced pullback is compatible with the simplicial structure, and the locally split Čech descent of [F1] for the principal bundle $P_N\to X_N$ identifies the Cartesian-cohomology derived category of the nerve of $P_N$ with $D_c^b(X_N;k)$. Composing with $Q_N$ gives the identification of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory of $D_c^{[b,a]}(X_N;k)$ in the stated range: an equivariant object $A$ corresponds to the triple $(Q_N(A),\ p_N^*A\cong q_N^*Q_N(A))$, and conversely a triple whose frame pullback comes from $X$ arises from an equivariant object. The bounded Hom comparison of [F3] is induced by pullback along $p_N$ and the descent equivalence, hence carries composition to composition; at $m=0$ it is a ring comparison $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ for objects in the interval, and retract closure is inherited from [F3].

**Idempotent completeness.** Let $e:K\to K$ be an idempotent endomorphism of a bounded object $K\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. Form the telescope in the bounded-below derived category of all simplicial sheaves: let $S=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}K$ be the countable sum with the shift map $1-\operatorname{shift}(e):S\to S$ sending the $j$-th summand to the $j$-th summand by $\mathrm{id}$ and to the $(j+1)$-st by $-e$, and let $T=\operatorname{Cone}(1-\operatorname{shift}(e))$. Countable coproducts in $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ exist levelwise and are exact, and the cone is levelwise, so $H^j(T)=\operatorname{colim}_j\bigl(H^j(K)\xrightarrow{H^j(e)}H^j(K)\xrightarrow{H^j(e)}\cdots\bigr)=\operatorname{im}H^j(e)$: the colimit of an idempotent is its image, and because $H^j(e)$ is an idempotent endomorphism of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(K)$ its image is a direct summand. The image of an idempotent of a simplicial sheaf is again a simplicial sheaf, is bounded, is Cartesian because it is a summand of a Cartesian object, and restricts on $X$ to the image of the idempotent $H^j(e)_0$, a summand of a constructible sheaf and hence constructible of finite rank. Thus $T$ is an object of the bounded-below ambient derived category with bounded Cartesian constructible cohomology, and by truncation it defines an object of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. The first-summand inclusion $i:K\to T$ satisfies $ie=i$ by the telescope relations, and the map $S\to K$ with every component $e$ annihilates $1-\operatorname{shift}(e)$, so the triangle yields $p:T\to K$ with $pi=e$. Then $ip$ is an isomorphism on cohomology, hence by [F2] an isomorphism; replacing $p$ by $p(ip)^{-1}$ gives $ip=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $pi=e$, splitting the idempotent inside $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. Hence the category is idempotent complete.

**Triangulated, locally small, conservative.** Steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 exhibit the ambient category and its Hom groups, the triangulated structure of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$, and conservativity of restriction; step 2.2 gives the finite resolution identification and the degree-zero ring and retract comparisons. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is asserted or used.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 give the triangulated, locally small model with conservative restriction and the finite resolution comparisons; step 2.3 gives idempotent completeness. AC is consumed exactly as recorded in [A1].
